methods.dating_method: PhyloBayes / FastDate; one of 10 cross-validated chronograms (fb_8 default fossil calibration scheme). The full Varga 2019 megaphylogeny has 5,284 ML tips; this 543-taxon dated backbone is the largest archived chronogram derivative.
methods.note: Installed as atlas sub-clade tree 2026-05-19 from Dryad 10.5061/dryad.gc2k9r9 (PhyloBayes_FastDate.zip → PhyloBayes_output/fb_8.chain_sample.chronogram). trees.derivation:
Derived from the 301-tip Arnold 2010 10kTrees v3 MCC by pruning to a
single representative per species (smallest numeric tip ID under each
Genus_species). 9.6% subspecies-level redundancy in the original tree
(34 subspecies-suffixed tips like Gorilla_gorilla_gorilla).
Reproducible via scripts/derive_species_tree.py.

~55,000 described mites and ticks (paraphyletic group within
Arachnida: Acariformes + Parasitiformes). Estimated total may
exceed 1 million species. Klimov 2018 (Annu Rev Entomol) is the
most recent dated phylogenomic synthesis but covers only ~200
species across the two superorders. Pepato 2018 also produced
dated Acariformes framework. NO atlas-scale species tree exists —
mite phylogenetics is highly fragmented across families.

superorders (Acariformes via Pepato 2018; Parasitiformes via Klimov
2018) but no combined Acari-wide species-level chronogram. With
>100k undescribed species expected, comprehensive coverage is
unrealistic.

methods.dating_method:
Chronosynth — summarizes node ages from dated input trees. Expanded from
Datelife concepts; uses input node-age sets as calibrations and smooths
over the topology. The dated synthesis tree is built by sampling 100
random taxon-addition trees per Clements taxonomy year, dating each via
Chronosynth, then summarizing to a single MCC tree.
methods.support_typical:
Per-branch support is the number of input studies supporting that branch:
grey (0 conflicting studies) → dull red (1-4) → bright red (5+ conflicting).
14% of branches conflict with the majority of input studies. 3,781 branches
(34% of the tree) have at least one conflicting input study.
methods.divergence_ci_note:
CIs on node dates from the 100-tree taxon-addition sample. The synthesis
explicitly summarizes uncertainty across input studies. The atlas ships
only the MCC consensus.

inputs.note:
9,239 / 10,824 species (85%) have direct phylogenetic information from
input studies. The remaining 15% are placed by addTaxa using
Clements/Birds-of-the-World taxonomic constraints. This is unusual
relative to other partitions in the atlas (typically all tips come
from sequence data); the audit surfaces this fact as a methodological
consideration when interpreting species-level placement uncertainty.

caveats.summary: Chronogram referenced in the paper was never deposited
caveats.detail:
Orr et al. 2022 (Sci Adv) ran MCMCtree with 18 fossil calibrations
under a relaxed-rates molecular clock and present the resulting
time-calibrated tree as Fig 2 of the published paper. The
chronogram FILE itself, however, is not in either of the paper's
data archives — Dryad (10.5061/dryad.2v6wwpzp9) holds only the
18-locus sequence alignments and two ML topology Newick files
(SI_Fig1 BIG, SI_Fig2 TRIMMED), and the Zenodo record
(10.5281/zenodo.5721078) contains only 311 MB of SEM image cards.
The atlas-canonical Bryozoa tree shown here is therefore the
species-level pruning of the SI_Fig2 ML topology (no branch
lengths in absolute time). Recovering the chronogram for atlas
use would require contacting the corresponding author.

described in the paper (MCMCtree, 18 fossil calibrations, Fig 2) but
was never deposited as a Newick file — verified 2026-05-19 against
Dryad (10.5061/dryad.2v6wwpzp9, alignments + ML trees only) and
Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.5721078, SEM images only). See caveats above.
Waeschenbach 2012 is the only alternative dated bryozoan tree
archived publicly, but with much smaller taxon coverage.

estimated_high.note:
TTWG does not publish a true-diversity bound. The 370 figure allows
~10 undescribed/cryptic species. Turtles are extremely well-described
(~1 new species per year, mostly subspecies elevations); the actual
cryptic-diversity reserve is small. Honest upper bound is within ~5%
of described.

interval_provenance.auditor_note:
Turtles intervals are heuristic. Like Birds and Mammals, turtles are a
well-catalogued clade — TTWG publishes a checklist, not a diversity
estimate. The 370 placeholder shouldn't be visually equated with the
paper-published ranges that exist for poorly-described clades
(Insects 2.6M-7.8M from Stork 2018, etc).

methods.substitution_model:
MrBayes: per-partition substitution models selected with model selection.
BEAST divergence-time run: Hasegawa-Kishino-Yano (HKY) for each partition
(chosen for MCMC performance, not strict model fit).
methods.dating_method:
BEAST 1.8.2 with uncorrelated lognormal relaxed clock; birth-death tree
prior; estimated on a reduced one-individual-per-species version of the
dataset.
methods.support_typical:
Posterior probability = 1 on the major deep splits (Cryptodira / Pleurodira,
all 14 currently recognized families monophyletic). Tree captures all 14
families and 98% of genera; species-level support varies, not summarized
in a single number.

findings.issue:
The CSV says "13 loci for 294 species". The Thomson 2021 paper reports
15 loci and 279 of 348 living species (80%). The original filename
"thomson2021_turtle_mcc_294sp.tre" preserves the 294 figure — possibly
from an early Dryad release that included subspecies in the species count.
findings.fix:
Manual reconciliation needed. Confirm whether the shipped MCC tree is the
same as the paper's 591-individual MCC (which corresponds to 279 species
+ outgroups) or an alternative Dryad version. Update methods_brief
accordingly.

findings.issue:
Tree has 593 tip positions and 329 unique numeric IDs. The dictionary
maps these IDs to names that include subspecies (e.g. Terrapene_ornata_luteola)
and locality codes (e.g. Kinosternon_dunni_K38). This means the tree's
"species" coverage is ambiguous without de-duplication.
findings.fix:
Web app should surface this ("593 tips covering ~279 species across
multiple individuals; some tips are subspecies"). Already partially
captured by the existing notes field in data_provenance.csv: "Multiple
individuals per species; displayed coverage is capped at 100%".
